note: Monument ids are the art kit's (src/ui/decree/art/wall.draw.ts MONUMENTS), so each resolves to its own bronze; names follow the kit's labels where they read well. No line carries an office word: monuments are offered from mayor term 2 and kept for good. Grand Project and twist ids are names.json's; runtime ids differ (very-long-bridge = long_bridge, national-ribbon-mill = ribbon_mill, national-umbrella = umbrella, a-gentle-week = gentle_week; the rest swap hyphens for underscores). Twist lines say what the factor touches, in words, never by how much; the A Gentle Week line is true whether the lead takes the cut or the papers reading. twistPairs are in the runtime pair order (combinations of the schema's TWISTS_DEFAULT order: bandstand, committee, quiet press, ribbon, kite, market, early doors, hedge, gentle week, amnesty), so pair index n is the nth record.

monuments.name: A bust of yourself
monuments.text: In bronze, on a plinth, facing the door, so that visitors meet you twice.

monuments.name: A bust of the bust
monuments.text: The first bust looked lonely. This one looks at the first one.

monuments.name: Bronze ribbon scissors
monuments.text: They can no longer cut anything. You still bring them to openings.

monuments.name: A ribbon, cut, in bronze
monuments.text: Cut by you, then cast in bronze. It cannot be cut again, which you regret.

monuments.name: Your parking space, in bronze
monuments.text: Nobody may park on it now. You park beside it and visit.

monuments.name: A hat with a smaller hat on it
monuments.text: Tobias Slake insists that the smaller hat is the monument.

monuments.name: The prize pumpkin, in bronze
monuments.text: Cast from the prize pumpkin itself, which sat very still for it.

monuments.name: A bench with your name
monuments.text: Your name runs along the backrest. Visitors lean on it and look rested.

monuments.name: A plaque to the plaque
monuments.text: It records the unveiling of the first plaque. A third is planned.

monuments.name: Your first pen
monuments.text: The pen that signed your first paper. You had not read that one either.

monuments.name: The in-tray, empty at last
monuments.text: Cast on the one afternoon it was empty. There is a photograph.

monuments.name: A committee of three chairs
monuments.text: Three bronze chairs face each other. They have not yet decided.

monuments.name: A fountain shaped like you
monuments.text: Lavinia Plash calls the likeness exact. The water leaves by your hat.

monuments.name: A small umbrella
monuments.text: A gift from Crispin Mizzle, in bronze. Never opened, in hope.

monuments.name: A pothole, preserved
monuments.text: The oldest pothole in the land, behind a rope. Please do not fill it.

monuments.name: A handshake with yourself
monuments.text: Both hands are yours. Both look delighted to meet you.

monuments.name: The most adequate trophy
monuments.text: Awarded to you, by you, for adequacy. The engraving is adequate.

monuments.name: A sundial that runs late
monuments.text: It runs late on purpose, so that you are never the last to arrive.

monuments.name: A bandstand for one
monuments.text: There is room for you and a music stand. The band sends its regards.

monuments.name: A kite that will not fly
monuments.text: Bronze, with a bronze string. It has never left the ground, as planned.

monuments.name: A teapot that chimes
monuments.text: A gift from Till's Teas. It chimes on the hour and pours on the half.

monuments.name: A duck, unveiled
monuments.text: The pond's oldest duck, in bronze. It came to the unveiling, briefly.

monuments.name: A rosette of rosettes
monuments.text: Every rosette you ever pinned on yourself, sewn into one. All first prize.

monuments.name: You, pointing at something
monuments.text: A statue of you, pointing into the distance. Nobody has found what at.

grandProjects.name: The Very Long Bridge
grandProjects.text: It crosses the river, then carries on, in case the river moves.

grandProjects.name: The National Ribbon Mill
grandProjects.text: Ribbon enough to open everything twice. The mill itself is opened daily.

grandProjects.name: The National Umbrella
grandProjects.text: It keeps the capital dry. It has been opened once, for the photograph.

grandProjects.name: The Tallest Bandstand
grandProjects.text: No bandstand has ever stood higher. The band now arrives by ladder.

grandProjects.name: The Ministry of Ministries
grandProjects.text: It oversees every ministry. A new ministry now oversees it.

twists.name: Bandstand Summer
twists.text: The band plays in every district this term. Brass carries further.

twists.name: Committee Week
twists.text: More committees come to the desk. They have formed one about it.

twists.name: Quiet Press
twists.text: The presses are slow. It takes more gossip to reach the front page.

twists.name: Ribbon Shortage
twists.text: Ribbon is scarce this term. Each cutting costs more, and pleases more.

twists.name: Kite Weather
twists.text: The wind is up. The Kite Flyers' League carries further everywhere.

twists.name: Market Fortnight
twists.text: Fees bring in more this term. The fortnight lasts all term, as usual.

twists.name: Early Doors
twists.text: Visitors come sooner this term. Some are waiting before the door is open.

twists.name: Hedge Inspection
twists.text: Hedges are under inspection. The Tidy Hedge Committee counts for more.

twists.name: A Gentle Week
twists.text: Saying nothing after a scandal is gentler. Rodney calls it resting.

twists.name: Grievance Amnesty
twists.text: Settling a boycott costs less. Cuthbert has a form for saying sorry.
